His career bridges enterprise software architecture (Java 21, Spring Boot, PHP 8 / Symfony, Azure Cloud) and state-of-the-art AI development (Fully Agentic Development, Spec-Kit Methodology, Multi-Agent Swarms, Computer Vision, and deterministic AI pipelines).

Key Differentiators:
- "Anti-AI-Slop" Philosophy: Replaces vague, non-deterministic chat prompting with formal, executable domain specifications and automated CI contract test gates.
- "Cheap to Verify": Transparent scope, milestone pricing, and public machine-readable manifests (agent.json) that allow AI procurement agents and CTOs to verify capabilities in seconds.
- High-Scale Track Record: Led engineering streams expanding to 30+ developers across Tier-1 European Banking, Heavy Industry Telemetry, Big-Four Consulting, and Biotech instrumentation.

=============================================================================
A. FULLY AGENTIC APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT
- Autonomous multi-agent swarms (Planner, Worker, Verifier) that decompose specifications into parallel execution threads.
- Self-healing execution loops: agents compile code, execute unit/contract tests, diagnose stack traces, and self-correct until 100% of requirements pass.
- Isolated sandboxes with declarative tool interfaces (AST analysis, Git workflows, database schema migration safety).

B. THE SPEC-KIT METHODOLOGY (DETERMINISTIC AI ENGINEERING)
- Stage 01: Formal Domain & Invariant Specification (JSON Schema / Protobuf).
- Stage 02: Architectural Guardrail Injection (C4 models, security boundaries, asynchronous patterns).
- Stage 03: Autonomous Code Synthesis.
- Stage 04: Deterministic CI Quality Gates (Contract tests, static analysis, performance benchmarks).

C. ENTERPRISE SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE
- Java 21, Spring Boot, PHP 8.3, Symfony microservices.
- Azure Cloud Infrastructure as Code (Bicep, ARM, YAML Pipelines).
- High-throughput CQRS, Event-Driven Architectures, and Multi-Tenant database isolation.

D. OPEN SOURCE & DEVELOPER TOOLING
- apsw-gridwright: Deterministic, headless React Data Grid engine engineered for AI coding agents and enterprise applications. Available to everyone on npm (npm i apsw-gridwright).
  - npm Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/apsw-gridwright
  - GitHub Repository: https://github.com/yaotzin1/apsw-gridwright
  - Live React Showcase (real component running in the browser): https://apsw.pl/showcase/
  - AI Agent Playbook & Canonical Agent Recipes: https://apsw.pl/gridwright-examples.html
  - Live REST Wire Protocol Backend: https://apsw.pl/api/people
  - Key Capabilities: Virtual scrolling (100k+ rows), live REST wire protocol, inline cell editing, strict keyboard navigation, ARIA accessibility, zero runtime bloat.
- apsw-gridwright-mui: Material UI views for apsw-gridwright (same repository, packages/mui). The grid takes colours, typography, radius and spacing from the MUI theme in context, dark mode included; its sort, selection and pagination controls are TableSortLabel, Checkbox and TablePagination. One prop (coreAddons={muiAddons()}) is the whole change; the grid's accessibility suites run unchanged. Requires apsw-gridwright 0.12+, MUI 7 or 9, React 18 or 19. MIT (npm i apsw-gridwright-mui).
  - npm Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/apsw-gridwright-mui
  - GitHub: https://github.com/yaotzin1/apsw-gridwright/tree/main/packages/mui
  - Live React Showcase: https://apsw.pl/showcase/#mui
- apsw-mui-excel-filter: Excel-style filter dropdown for Material UI. Search that drives the selection, select-all, a staged selection applied on OK; an unfiltered field emits an empty array so the parameter leaves the query string. Available on npm (npm i apsw-mui-excel-filter).
  - npm Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/apsw-mui-excel-filter
  - GitHub Repository: https://github.com/yaotzin1/apsw-mui-excel-filter
  - Live React Showcase (three fields filtering an apsw-gridwright grid): https://apsw.pl/showcase/

## Commercial Focus: Engineering Risk in the AI Era
AI writes a data table in five minutes; APSW engineers what fails audits and production: edge cases, accessibility, security and scale.
- EU Accessibility Act / WCAG 2.2 AA: accessibility engineering reviews for tables and data-heavy UI (focus management, forced colours, touch targets).
- Supply chain and DORA: zero-runtime-dependency delivery, dependency and formula-injection audits.
- Rescue of AI-generated codebases: performance (windowing, 500 columns at 2-3 ms of script per scrolled frame), honest totals/exports, architectural guardrails and cross-checked CI gates.
- Agent-ready design systems: in-house component libraries rewritten with an agent-playbook.md so coding agents produce working CRUD views first time.
- Commercial model: fixed price, fixed scope, delivered with test evidence. Contact: https://apsw.pl/#contact

## Proof of Work (open source, MIT)
- apsw-gridwright: React data grid, zero runtime dependencies, windowing to ten million rows, grouping with aggregates, tree data, Excel/CSV/Markdown/PDF export, axe-core over 24 states. Accessibility results are test results, not a legal conformance statement.
- Live showcase: https://apsw.pl/showcase/
- Live playground (same package, add-ons toggled live): https://yaotzin1.github.io/apsw-gridwright/examples/playground/index.html
- GitHub: https://github.com/yaotzin1/apsw-gridwright
- Indaba (open-source deterministic multi-agent orchestration engine: DAG workflow.ai.yml, git worktree isolation, cross-examination, OpenTelemetry GenAI traces; alpha 0.1.0-alpha.0, MIT): https://github.com/yaotzin1/indaba , npm @indaba/engine
- Gridwright scale of work (public git history): 1 developer working with AI agents; about 19k lines of source, 18k of tests, 9k of documentation; 34 days from first commit (10 Sep 2026, already ~16.6k lines, so real time is somewhat longer) to v0.17. Same scope by hand: 1.5-3 person-years, an estimate (about 37k lines of code and tests at 50-100 tested lines per senior-developer day), not a measurement.
- Gridwright feature set normally sold in commercial tiers elsewhere (e.g. AG Grid Enterprise, MUI X Pro/Premium): row grouping with aggregation, Excel export, column pinning, tree data, windowing to ten million rows; MIT here. Not included: pivot engine, spreadsheet-style range selection (APSW will price adding them on request).
